question: A 57-year-old man comes to the physician with a 3-month history of right flank pain. Urinalysis shows 60 RBC/hpf. Renal ultrasound shows a 3 cm, well-defined mass in the upper pole of the right kidney. A photomicrograph of a section of the resected mass is shown. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Right flank pain" -> "Urinalysis shows 60 RBC/hpf" -> "Renal ultrasound shows a 3 cm, well-defined mass in the upper pole of the right kidney" -> "Photomicrograph of resected mass shown" -> "Possible diagnosis: Clear cell renal carcinoma" -> 70%

CHAIN: "Right flank pain" -> "Urinalysis shows 60 RBC/hpf" -> "Renal ultrasound shows a 3 cm, well-defined mass in the upper pole of the right kidney" -> "Photomicrograph of resected mass shown" -> "Possible diagnosis: Oncocytoma" -> 60%

CHAIN: "Right flank pain" -> "Urinalysis shows 60 RBC/hpf" -> "Renal ultrasound shows a 3 cm, well-defined mass in the upper pole of the right kidney" -> "Photomicrograph of resected mass shown" -> "Possible diagnosis: Chromophobe renal cell carcinoma" -> 50%
analysis: Based on the clinical presentation of right flank pain, hematuria, and the imaging findings of a well-defined mass in the upper pole of the right kidney, along with the photomicrograph showing characteristic features, the most likely diagnosis is clear cell renal carcinoma.
